messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: P0 - auth-service failing token validation for multiple customers. Symptoms: JWTs rejected with 'kid' lookup failure and 401 spikes. service=auth-service env=prod

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #PD-49217 - acknowledged by maria.ops

maria.ops: Acked. I'm on it. seeing ~15% 401 rate across edge LB. Customers reporting login failures. @karen.support please start collecting customer IDs and any support tickets.

karen.support: On it. Opened a tkt tracker doc and pinged accounts. will paste affected customer IDs here as we gather them.

jamal.sre: Jumping in — checking auth-service logs. Querying jwks cache + verification errors. quick grep: `grep "kid" /var/log/auth/*.log | head` shows repeated `kid not found in JWKS`.

sophia.auth: Did we just rotate keys? I deployed a build last night that updated key publishing. Checking JWKS endpoint now: `curl -sS https://auth.redwood.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'` returns only one kid: "k3-old".

maria.ops: Our tokens have kid=k3-rotated in headers. So mismatch. Who pushed key rotation? @sophia.auth any config that could have unpublished the rotated key?

sophia.auth: I see a config roll last night that should have published both keys during rollover, but the publiser worker crashed. Investigating. logs show: `publiser: failed to register new JWK -> timeout calling KMS`

jamal.sre: For immediate mitigation can we accept tokens with unknown kid by fetching signing keys lazily? Risky but might reduce customer impact. Thoughts?

sophia.auth: We can enable a permissive fallback: if kid not found, attempt to verify against previous key set by JWK thumbprint or attempt legacy key. I'll push a small patch to auth-service to try existing cached keys as fallback. Deploying to canary now.

maria.ops: Good. Also, can we proxy a copy of the new key at a static path so tokens with rotated kid validate? Might be faster than resolving KMS.

sophia.auth: Pushing quick fallback: auth-service will, on kid-miss, call internal service `keystore/legacy-lookup` which reads last-known keys from blob store. Patching now.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step executed: applied temporary permissive validation. Documentation: https://runbook.internal/auth#jwks-mismatch -> step 3 executed by sophia.auth

jamal.sre: Canary shows 401 rate dropped to ~2% after fallback enabled. Rolling to 25% traffic now.

maria.ops: Good. Karen, any new customer reports?

karen.support: Still seeing a handful of tickets but reduced. Flagging one enterprise customer that had continuous failures (acct: AcmeCo). Notified their AM.

sophia.auth: Root cause: KMS key registration timeout during nightly rotation job. The registration script assumed idempotent response; when KMS returned transient 503, publisher aborted without retry, so rotated key never entered JWKS. Fix: add exponential retries + circuit breaker. Will open PR.

jamal.sre: Action items: 1) keep permissive fallback for 2h while we roll fixed publisher, 2) re-run registration job to publish missing key, 3) sweep logs for tokens that failed to validate and correlate to customers for postmortem.

maria.ops: Agreed. Also start a private Slack channel for coordination with support and oncall-next for handoff. I'll create it in a sec and invite folks.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: escalation to oncall-next scheduled in 40m for handoff to day team.

sophia.auth: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/auth/pulls/618 - adds retries and alerts if key registration fails 3x. Will deploy to prod after review. Running manual registration now: `./scripts/register_jwk.sh --key=k3-rotated` returns 200. JWKS now includes k3-rotated.

jamal.sre: After manual register and full roll, 401s back to baseline (<0.1%). Rolling fallback removal to avoid long-term risk. Removing permissive mode from canary.

maria.ops: Confirmed metrics: auth 5xx/401 spikes resolved. Support queue declining. Notifying stakeholders.

karen.support: Notified AcmeCo and three other enterprise customers. Sent temporary mitigation summary and ETA for root cause fix.

maria.ops: Preparing brief incident note for postmortem: timeline, root cause (KMS transient 503 during key rotation, publisher missing retry), mitigation (fallback, manual register), follow-ups (retry logic, alerting on publisher failures, test for rotation). Assigning owners: sophia.auth -> fix + PR; jamal.sre -> log sweep + metrics alert; karen.support -> customer comms.

oncall-next: Acknowledge handoff. Will monitor for 4 hours, follow up on any regressions. Thanks team.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: Severity=P1 -> downgraded; duration ~23m. Please file a postmortem ticket and link it here.

maria.ops: Filing postmortem now. Thanks everyone for quick response.
